authoredNote: Lines re-read off the analyzer output for THIS fixture (31, 37, 45, 52, 69, 74, 78, 94, 104). The `factory` row at 45 is the 2026-10-18 addition; the absent-owner control moved to `viaUntypedFactory` so both directions stay pinned without line scoping.
rationale: THE RECEIVER'S TYPE ON A MEMBER CALL, now covering SIX syntactic forms with an evidence class per form: `const c = new Widget()` (assignment) · `const d: Widget = make()` (annotation — an EXPLICIT annotation beats the factory's inferred return, and this row is the precedence pin) · `private inner: Widget` + `this.inner.m()` (this) · `function f(w: Widget)` + `w.m()` (param) · `const e = make()` with `make(): Widget` in the same file (factory) · one-hop member of a typed parameter and of a destructured parameter (param). THE CONTROLS: an unannotated factory (`untypedMake()`), an unannotated parameter and a member-of-typed-parameter negative shape must carry NO owner — pinned by positive rows with no owner and by field-scoped FORBIDS asserting the `meta.owner` value is absent (a forbid on the bare row would fire on the legitimate unowned row; a forbid carrying `meta.owner: Widget` only fails if the rule over-claims). STALE-CONTROL UPDATE (task-9 ruling, 2026-10-18): CONTROL 2 used to assert `const e = make()` states no type. That premise was TRUE before the factory-return class and is FALSE after (`make()` IS annotated `: Widget`). Coverage was not weakened: that line is now an EXPECTED factory row, and the absent-owner control is a genuinely unannotated factory (`untypedMake`).
